review_basis: Independent static IL/native control-flow review and isolated decoder emulation; malware was not executed against the host or its remote endpoints.

samples.identification: Self-named ExtremeRansomwareBotnet, managed input recorder and ransom locker
evidence: Main (MethodDef 0x0600001a) calls ShowLockScreen, BlockInput(true), InstallPersistence and StartKeylogger and schedules the surveillance workers.
StartKeylogger (0x06000025) passes HookCallback to SetWindowsHookEx with WH_KEYBOARD_LL=13; HookCallback records WM_KEYDOWN virtual keys with File.AppendAllText.
The polling thread (0x0600006b) checks GetAsyncKeyState's 0x8000 bit for keys through 255 and appends timestamped key names.
ContinuousScreenshot (0x06000028) copies the primary screen and saves JPEGs; ClipboardMonitor reads and records clipboard text.
ContinuousDataExfiltration.MoveNext (0x060000a2) reads the key/clipboard logs, packages their contents into records and calls SendToC2.
SendToC2.MoveNext (0x060000a4) serializes records into the data form field and supplies FormUrlEncodedContent to HttpClient.PostAsync.
USBWorm (0x0600002a) copies Application.ExecutablePath to ready removable drives and writes autorun.inf with an executable open directive.
BypassUAC (0x0600003b) writes its executable path and empty DelegateExecute to HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command and launches fodhelper.exe.
limits: RealEncryption targets Desktop/TestFolder. EncryptAES assigns a 14-byte IV to AES, so encryption throws before the replacement write/delete. Detection retains the attempted-replacement claim.
Blackcat and HiddenTears wording is self-assigned and does not establish either malware family.
The new input-exfiltration signature requires both the recognized recorder and send-related references but does not bind CLR values across methods; its severity is suspicious.
samples.change: Add file-keylogger log-read/JSON/form-POST co-occurrence coverage without claiming a statically bound send.

evidence: The outer PE's entry reaches the loader at 0x401170. Its native restore/handoff abandons the original frame and transfers to a recovered buffer; stock UPX cannot unpack it.
The buffer at outer VA 0x42b3d0 has a 179432-byte length prefix and a raw Snappy stream. Independent bounded decompression recovers 179432 bytes, including a PE at buffer offset 0x2e8.
Recovered PE 0x4110ef locates Firefox/Thunderbird installation paths and 0x410f11 resolves NSS and SQLite functions into a dispatch table.
Recovered PE 0x41153f/0x41165f traverse profile directories and open signons.sqlite. 0x4114d2 selects encryptedusername and encryptedpassword from moz_logins and dispatches each row to 0x411258.
Recovered PE 0x41119f calls NSSBase64_DecodeBuffer and PK11SDR_Decrypt on those values. 0x411258 packages the host, username and password into serialized Mozilla credential records.
Recovered PE 0x401923 uses AdjustKernelTableFromSSDTSpace2 as an RC4 key-scheduling input. This is not evidence that an SSDT helper executes.
Recovered PE 0x40bfc5/0x40c2dd implement buffered FTP writes through dynamically resolved InternetWriteFile; the payload also implements raw-input recording.
limits: The outer specimen lacks the chrome.exe resource required by the older Chrome-disguise composite. Its verdict rests on recovered credential-theft code, not the original filename.
The packed query atom now requires binary breaks in both truncated words and no longer duplicates intact plaintext moz_logins SQL.
The hostile packed Firefox composite now requires the concealed native handoff as well as NSS/query fragments.
samples.change: Tighten packed Firefox evidence and rename the family-specific SSDT string as a cipher-key observation.

evidence: Startup 0x404551 reconstructs configuration through 0x4032c0 and starts the tasking loop at 0x403dcd.

0x4032c0 reconstructs four configuration fragments. 0x4059a6 XORs bytes with 0x42 before decompression at 0x404b97. Isolated emulation recovered a 1580-byte configuration with remote servers i.assmio.com and m.assmio.com, ports 80/443/5432 and a WINWORD self-copy name.
The worker at 0x4037cb receives HTTP data through the dynamically resolved WinINet wrapper, validates the binary header checksum and dispatches header field +0x10 over command IDs 1000 through 1019.
Command handlers at 0x403a45/0x403a58 pass the received payload at +0x20 to 0x403466/0x403662 for execution. 0x403466 captures pipe output and returns it into the response built by 0x4025da.
0x404e6a also creates a hidden cmd.exe with piped standard input/output; 0x404ff4 writes received commands into that process and 0x405077 captures output.
0x403256 reaches 0x40317d, which gets its own module path, formats cmd /c ping 127.0.0.1 -n 1&del with that path, and launches the deletion command through WinExec.
Version resources claim Microsoft Word / Microsoft Office 2016 / WINWORD.exe, inconsistent with the tasking implant.
limits: A single loopback ping does not establish a delay; the two self-delete rules were moved from file/delay to file/script with consumers updated.
The collector's elex_wannacry label is not used for attribution. No ransomware-encryption claim is made.
samples.change: Preserve the confirmed RAT/self-delete coverage while correcting script-mediated deletion placement.

controls.purpose: Renamed positives, source/transport-role ablations, packed-fragment and hidden-handoff near misses, inert PE reference controls, and self-delete move/reference preservation.
controls.ablation_scope: Removing a static signature leg is not a benign verdict on the modified specimen.
